problem: Ed25519 response attestation proved coordinator origin, git SHA, service, and key identity, but a valid signed response was not explicitly bound to the worker requestId. A previously valid response from the same service/SHA/key could therefore be replayed against a different request unless higher layers noticed the mismatch.

reviews.preferred: bind requestId into the signed attestation context and require the expected requestId during verification
reviews.reason: Request identity becomes part of the cryptographic statement while preserving durable same-request retry semantics.

reviews.preferred: fail closed when request binding is expected but absent or mismatched
reviews.reason: This prevents a valid coordinator signature from becoming reusable evidence for another request.

reviews.preferred: extend the existing Ed25519 payload instead of adding a second signature or network attestation service
reviews.reason: No additional qrexec round trip, negligible payload growth, and no new process or key lifecycle.

alternatives.name: rely on service/SHA/key binding only
alternatives.reason: Authenticates origin but not request-response correlation.

alternatives.name: add a second HMAC over requestId and response
alternatives.reason: The worker already knows the transport HMAC secret, so it would not provide coordinator-origin evidence.

alternatives.name: external attestation daemon
alternatives.reason: Adds latency, policy, lifecycle, and operational failure modes without being necessary for per-request binding.

expected_effects.correctness: Signed responses can be matched to the exact logical worker request.
expected_effects.robustness: Missing legacy request binding fails closed when the caller requires request correlation.
expected_effects.latency: No extra qrexec calls; only a few bytes added to the signed payload.
expected_effects.resources: Negligible CPU and memory change relative to the existing Ed25519 verification.
expected_effects.regression_risk: Low at the primitive layer because request binding is opt-in until the qrexec service/harness integration is switched over.

added: successful verification for the matching requestId
rejection when the same signed response is verified against another requestId
fail-closed rejection when request binding is required but absent
qa.remaining: Wire the qrexec coordinator service to sign the authenticated envelope requestId and make the worker harness always verify expectedRequestId before recording attestation evidence.

lessons: Origin authentication and request-response correlation are separate properties.
A cryptographically valid response can still be unsafe evidence if it is reusable across logical requests.
Durable retries should reuse the same requestId, which is compatible with request-bound attestation and keeps committed-response recovery idempotent.
